_doc: The NEUTRAL registration for every enforcing hook in this repository.
ONE SOURCE, THREE REGISTRATIONS. The hook SCRIPTS live once, at
`.claude/hooks/<name>.js`, and all three CLIs invoke that same path — what
differs is only the manifest each one reads, and the event names each one
uses. `scripts/project_coc.mjs` derives all three from this file, so adding
a hook is one entry here rather than three hand-edited settings files that
drift silently and each look authoritative.
`matchers` are CC tool names. Gemini renames the EVENTS (BeforeTool /
AfterTool) but not the tools; Codex fires on the Bash lane only, which is
recorded per-hook in `codex_coverage` rather than left for a reader to
discover when a guard turns out not to fire.
`timeout_ms` is the HARNESS timeout and is deliberately GREATER than each
hook's own internal budget, so a slow hook reaches its own fail-open path
and emits `{continue:true}` rather than being killed mid-check. A harness
timeout at or below the internal budget makes the fail-open branch
unreachable, which is the opposite of what it is for.

hooks.name: deployment-blast-radius
hooks.codex_coverage: full — the surface it guards IS the Bash lane
hooks.exceeds_core: core has no concept of a live client deployment; a core developer's blast radius is a branch

hooks.name: client-credential-containment
hooks.codex_coverage: PARTIAL — Codex hooks fire on Bash only, so the Write/Edit arm does not fire there. Named rather than assumed.
hooks.exceeds_core: core's secret scanning is about THIS repo's secrets; this is about a client's, compared against live environment values rather than shapes

hooks.name: source-absence-boundary
hooks.codex_coverage: PARTIAL — Bash lane only under Codex; the Write/Edit arm needs the MCP-guard surface.
hooks.exceeds_core: core's evidence-first rule assumes the source is readable. Here it is not, and the narrower position needs the stronger guard.

hooks.name: probe-before-claim
hooks.codex_coverage: PARTIAL — Bash lane only under Codex.
hooks.exceeds_core: core can only advise 'cite the endpoint'; this repository ships the instrument, so the obligation has something to bind to

hooks.name: probe-before-claim
hooks.note: the RECORD half. It writes a receipt from the probe's own output, so the receipt is an observation by the harness rather than a claim by the agent.

hooks.name: anchor-integrity
hooks.codex_coverage: NONE on the Codex Bash lane — its whole surface is file writes, which Codex hooks do not see. This is a real gap and is recorded here rather than discovered later.
hooks.exceeds_core: core's citation gate was measured blind to 25% of its corpus and silent about its denominator; this reports examined-vs-skipped on every emission
